capabilities._note: audio: none. Wan 2.2 makes no sound: every take is a mute mp4, whatever the shot's audio policy (it renders `silent`, with a note in the take), and assemble lays silence under it.

models._note: Glob patterns (case-insensitive) naming the files each model parameter of the binding takes, for the model identification that reads them; `family` is its id for the file header check (high vs low noise is decided by the name: the headers are identical). `model` is the high noise (first stage) model, `model_low` the low noise one. Tiers (docs/API.md): the models, text encoder and VAE are required; `loras` is the accelerator (lightx2v's T2V A14B 4-step pair), so without it a pass renders its `base` preset -- 20 / 10 steps at cfg 3.5, which is how this target shipped before 2026-09-22. `keep` makes a substitute share the wanted file's step count and noise stage.

template._note: Wan 2.2 14B (Fun VACE is built on the A14B pair): 4k+1 frames at 16 fps, trained on 81 frames (5 s), so a longer shot is a warning, and past 161 frames (10 s) it must be split. Width and height are multiples of 16 (WanVaceToVideo's step; its masks need /8); sizes that aren't legal are snapped down, then shrunk under 720p.

recipe._note: Identity: WanVaceToVideo's reference_image is ONE picture (the node takes the first of a batch, scales it to the render size with a centre crop, and conditions the clip on it as an extra leading latent frame, trimmed afterwards). It is composed at queue time from the shot's picked refs: one panel per subject (characters in `who:` order, then props and vehicles; a character's face panel on a single-character close-up, else its three-quarter body panel, as ltx2_ingredients), at the render size, on WHITE (VACE pads its references on a white canvas; comfy_nodes/h3_refsheet.py). The location plate is left off by default (`plate: false`: one scene next to the subjects reads as another subject; the prose describes the place). Every panel's file is required (blocked, as ltx2_ingredients); rendering anyway drops the missing ones, and a shot with none renders from the prompt alone (and its keyframes). Keyframes: shot:<id>:first / last are optional control frames, the standard VACE first/last recipe: a control video of the keyframe(s) with mid-grey frames between, and a mask that keeps the keyframes (0) and generates the rest (1). No sound: every policy renders silent and says so.

policy_fallback.why: Wan 2.2 makes no sound (lay the soundtrack in at the edit)

size_hints.character sheet: 4096x1024 or larger (horizontal 4-panel strip; one panel goes on the reference image)
size_hints.prop reference: 1024x1024 or larger, on a plain light background
size_hints.vehicle reference: 1024x1024 or larger, on a plain light background
size_hints.keyframe: the render size (any size works: it is scaled and centre-cropped to the frame)

binding._note: An API graph built for this target from ComfyUI's Wan nodes (no VACE workflow was saved): the Wan 2.2 Fun VACE high/low noise pair, each with shift 8, sampling steps [0, split) and [split, end) with KSamplerAdvanced (`stages`, as wan22_i2v), conditioned by one WanVaceToVideo (reference_image, and control_video / control_masks for keyframes, added by patch_graph), then TrimVideoLatent drops the reference's leading latent frame (the node's trim_latent output) before VAEDecode. No LoRA loaders: one per stage is inserted after that stage's UNETLoader when a profile names LoRAs (by `stage`, else *high_noise* / *low_noise*, else both). H3SaveShot takes the place of CreateVideo/SaveVideo (no audio input: the mp4 is mute) at the job's fps.

presets._note: The Wan 2.2 Fun VACE 14B fp8 pair with lightx2v's Wan2.2-Lightning T2V A14B 4-step LoRA (one per noise stage, routed by `stage`), which is the accelerator for these experts -- the I2V pair wan22_i2v uses does not fit them. 4 steps at cfg 1, euler / shift 8, split half-way. `base` is what a pass renders when the pair isn't installed: the 20 / 10 step cfg 3.5 settings this target shipped with, slower but needing no LoRA. Every release of the pair ships as high_noise_model / low_noise_model, so the variant is in the name you save it under: 250928 reads as more natural with finer detail, Seko V2 does better on stylised and synthetic work -- swap the names here to A/B them. The negative prompt is Wan's standard one, from ComfyUI's Wan templates.
